title: Day 14 — Finish the Driver, See the Data, Measure Tilt

slides.title: Finish the Driver, See the Data, Measure Tilt
slides.subtitle: ENGS 28 · Day 14 — In-Class

slides.title: Where we are
items: On Tuesday we wired the LSM303AGR onto the bus and verified the link.  Yesterday we saw how it works inside, and how to convert its readings to milli-g.
You drafted lsm303_AccelRegisterWrite() on paper, and worked out the two control-register settings from the datasheet.
slides.presenterNote: Settling; her Day 14 deck opens straight into the agenda.

slides.title: Agenda
items: Send x-y-z data to the screen, observe tilt
Plot in CoolTerm's chart view, observe shock and vibration
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 2 min with announcements.  Her slide 2's three items, plus the lab hand-off.

slides.title: The settings, committed and revealed
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 10 min: 1 the sixty-second table look, 4 the commit, 5 the reveal.  The look is the mitigation for unread reading; the reveal lands 0x77/0x00 on the same tables.

slides.title: Commit to the two settings
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 4 min, in writing.  The bytes go into AccelInit within the half hour.

slides.title: The settings, revealed
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 5 min.  REVEAL — after the commit.  Page back to the table slides as you derive each field; the rounds-3.9-to-4 clause is on the modes slide's note.

slides.title: Verify the wiring, stage the project
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 8 min: 3 the re-verify, 2 the exclude beat, 3 the staging worktime.  Never cut the exclude beat: the two-main() linker error is new to everyone.

slides.title: One main() per build: exclude whoami_test.c
Verify, download, exclude
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 3 min of worktime.  A board that fails the re-verify gets priority triage during Parts 3–5's worktime, one-to-one.

slides.title: Complete the driver
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 17 min: 2 what the file gives, 2 the silent attempt, 2 the reveal, 2 the write transfer, 3 the AccelInit walk, 4 the fill-and-build, 2 its reveal.

slides.title: RegisterWrite, revealed
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 2 min.  REVEAL — after the attempt.  One i2c1_memWrite() call; say why &data and why the count is 1.

slides.title: What that call puts on the wire
AccelInit: your two values go in
Fill in the two settings
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 4 min of worktime: both functions finished, project builds.

slides.title: AccelInit, filled in
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 2 min.  REVEAL — after the fill.  Binary or hex both fine; the binary shows the fields.

slides.title: Run it
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 18 min: 1 + 2 the read-before-you-run walk, 11 build-run-test, 4 worktime with the ladder up.  CRUCIAL step; checkpoint at the end of this Part, minute 58.  Never cut.

slides.title: Read accel_test.c before you run it
Stream your first acceleration data
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 11 min.  CHECKPOINT at the end of this Part (minute 58): a student not yet streaming gets the completed driver file, ONE-TO-ONE and not announced, and still runs their own board through the flip and rotate tests.  Their paper RegisterWrite was already graded by the reveal.

slides.title: If something is wrong, read the printout
Make it a library
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 6 min.  Day 10's promotion discipline, second device.

slides.title: Promote the driver to your library
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 6 min of worktime: rename, move to mylib, delete from Src, rebuild, re-run.

slides.title: Plot it
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 12 min: 3 the modification, 3 the chart view, 5 the experiments, 1 the plotter shot.  Cut order trims the experiments to flip-and-shake.

slides.title: Make the chart move
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 5 min.  Predict before each move; the shock test (bang the table) is the one nobody guesses right.

slides.title: Tilt
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 11 min: 2 the commit, 1 its reveal, 4 the single-axis geometry, 4 the two-axis answer.  If the clock is behind, compress the single-axis contrast: state, don't derive, why atan2 wins.

slides.title: Predict the readings at 30 degrees
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 2 min, in writing.

slides.title: The readings at 30 degrees
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 1 min.  REVEAL — after the commit.  Gravity redistributes; the vector's length never changes.

slides.title: One axis: the arcsine, and where it fails
Two axes: the arctangent, and atan2()
Floating point
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 13 min: 1 the integer recap, 2 float and math.h, 4 the cast commit, 2 its reveal, 1 round(), 3 the cost.  Never cut: Lab 7 Deliverable 3 dies without the cast-and-round mechanics.

slides.title: The integer conversion, one more look
Place the cast
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 4 min, committed in writing.  The BRR recall is in the task; pose it before anyone answers.

slides.title: The cast, placed
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 2 min.  REVEAL — after the commit.  Land the answer explicitly: (float) on the raw value, first in the chain; casting the finished expression is too late.

slides.title: Lab 7
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 5 min.  The hand-off; homework equals the pre-lab, already done.

slides.title: Begin Lab 7's wiring
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 5 min of buffer: start the shared-bus wiring with help in the room.  Absorbs overrun from Parts 4–5; first thing cut if the clock is behind.
